ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

Financial Overview for Fiscal Year 2024:
Net sales increased 11% to $638.0 billion in 2024, compared with $574.8 billion in 2023.
AWS segment sales increased 19% year-over-year to $107.6 billion, driven by accelerated enterprise workload migrations and customer adoption of generative AI services including Bedrock and custom Trainium2 chips.
North America segment sales increased 10% to $387.5 billion. International segment sales increased 9% to $142.9 billion.
Operating income was $68.6 billion in 2024, compared with operating income of $36.9 billion in 2023, reflecting substantial operational fulfillment efficiencies.
Operating cash flow increased 39% to $118.2 billion for the trailing twelve months.
Capital expenditures were $75.0 billion, reflecting heightened investments in AWS generative AI datacenters and custom silicon.

Global economic conditions, geopolitical conflicts, and international trade disputes materially affect our business.
A substantial majority of the Company's manufacturing is performed by outsourced partners in Greater China, India, and Southeast Asia.
Geopolitical tensions between the United States and China, potential tariff increases, cross-border data transfer restrictions, and supply chain disruptions could adversely affect hardware production, component costs, and consumer demand.

ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS

Our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be materially adversely affected by several key risk factors:
We rely on third-party foundry partners, primarily Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), to manufacture all of our semiconductor wafers.
Any disruption in TSMC's manufacturing capacity, geopolitical conflict in the Taiwan Strait, natural disasters, or export trade sanctions could severely impede our ability to supply our Hopper HGX architecture, Blackwell chips, and Data Center GPUs.
Because we are fabless, we do not own or operate semiconductor fabrication facilities. If TSMC is unable or unwilling to allocate sufficient advanced packaging (CoWoS) and wafer capacity to us, our revenue and gross margins would be harmed.
Furthermore, U.S. government export controls and licensing requirements on high-performance GPUs shipped to China and other designated countries have impacted and may continue to materially reduce our Data Center revenue.

PART II
